'''''Juniperus procumbens''''' is a [[species]] of shrub in the cypress [[family (botany)|family]] Cupressaceae, [[native species|native]] to Japan. This low-growing [[evergreen]] [[conifer]] is closely related to the Chinese juniper, ''[[Juniperus chinensis]]'', and is sometimes treated as a variety of it, as ''J. chinensis'' var. ''procumbens''.<ref name=farjon/><ref name=adams/>

==Description==
It is a [[prostrate shrub]], usually growing {{convert|20-30|cm|in|abbr=off|frac=2}} tall, occasionally {{convert| 50|cm|in|abbr=on}}; while it does not get very tall it can get quite wide, {{convert|2-4|m|ft|abbr=|frac=2}} across or more, with long prostrate branches. The branches tend to intertwine and form a dense mat. The [[leaves]] are arranged in [[decussate]] whorls of three; all the leaves are juvenile form, needle-like, {{Convert|6–8|mm|frac=16}} long and 1–1.5 mm broad, with two white [[stoma]]tal bands on the inner face. It is [[dioecious]] with separate male and female plants. The [[conifer cone|cones]] are berry-like, globose, 8–9 mm in diameter, dark blackish-brown with a pale blue-white waxy bloom, and contain two or three [[seed]]s (rarely one); they are mature in about 18 months. The male cones are 3–4 mm long, and shed their pollen in early spring. It produces cones of only one sex on each plant.<ref name=farjon/><ref name=adams/><ref name=gd>Gymnosperm Database: [http://www.conifers.org/cu/ju/procumbens.htm ''Juniperus procumbens'']</ref>

==Distribution==
The status of ''Juniperus procumbens'' as a wild plant is disputed. Some authorities treat it as [[endemism|endemic]] to high mountains on [[Kyūshū]] and a few other islands off southern Japan,<ref name=farjon>Farjon, A. (2005). ''Monograph of Cupressaceae and Sciadopitys''. Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew. {{ISBN|1-84246-068-4}}</ref> while others consider it native to the coasts of southern Japan (north to [[Chiba Prefecture]]) and also the southern and western coasts of [[Korea]].<ref name=adams>{{citation |author=Adams, R. P. |year=2014 |title=Junipers of the World |edition=4th |publisher=Trafford Publishing | isbn=978-1-4907-2325-9 |page=112 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=u3CSAgAAQBAJ}}</ref>{{Self-published inline|certain=yes|date=January 2018}}

==Cultivation and uses==

[[File:Juniperus procumbens.jpg|thumb|Juniperus procumbens being trained as a [[bonsai]]. Its contorted trunk lines add interest and drama to the artistic composition.]]
[[Image:Bonsai Juniperus procumbens.jpg|thumb|A bonsai specimen of 'Nana']]
Several [[cultivar]]s have been selected, the most widely grown being 'Nana', a slow-growing procumbent plant,<ref name=adams/><ref name=wcc>Welch, H. & Haddow, G. (1993). ''The World Checklist of Conifers''. {{ISBN|0-900513-09-8}}</ref> which in the [[UK]] has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web
| url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/98531/i-Juniperus-procumbens-i-Nana/Details
| title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Juniperus procumbens'' 'Nana' | access-date=14 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 56 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 14 March 2018}}</ref>  Others include 'Bonin Isles', a strong-growing mat-forming plant collected on the [[Bonin Islands]],<ref name=wcc/> and 'Green Mound', which may just be a renaming of 'Nana'.<ref name=wcc/> A variegated plant sold under the name ''J. procumbens'' 'Variegata' is actually a cultivar of ''J. chinensis'' misnamed.<ref name=wcc/> {{Clear|left}}
